newsitem.title: CANADA: Winter storm wreaks havoc in Ontario and Quebec.
newsitem.headline: Winter storm wreaks havoc in Ontario and Quebec.

text.p: A winter storm that blasted much of the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Quebec with freezing rain and blowing snow on Saturday wreaked havoc for motorists and left tens of thousands of residents without electricity.
Hydro-Quebec, the Quebec government utility that distributes most of the French speaking province's electricity, said 87,000 of its customers still had no power on Saturday.
Hydro-Quebec said 164 work crews would battle icy roads and freezing weather overnight on Saturday in an effort to restore electricity to those customers still affected by power outages.
"We made progress after the freezing rain, but the strong winds came and caused further outages," Hydro-Quebec spokeswoman Marie Archambault told Reuters.
In the region south of Montreal, the province's largest city, more than 200 hydro poles were downed. But the utility said none of its high-voltage transmission lines were affected.

The same storm caused problems for motorists and residents elsewhere. Quebec City, the provicial capital 171 miles (275 km) northeast of Montreal along the St. Lawrence River, was digging out from under 12 inches (30 cm) of new snow, with forecasters expecting another six inches (15 cm) by Sunday.

Near Quebec City, police used snowmobiles to rescue several stranded motorists. Communities along some of Quebec's major rivers, including the Chateauguay, Richelieu and Yamaska Rivers outside Montreal and St. Francois River eastward toward the province's Eastern Townships were on alert for flooding.

In Ontario, Canada's most populated province, freezing rain and high winds were blamed for several fatal highway accidents. Officials in the southern part of the province were concerned about possible flooding from rivers swollen by unseasonal rains and early ice break-up.
Officials in Toronto, Canada's biggest city, declared an extreme cold weather alert as temperatures were forecast to plummet to 7 degrees fahrenheit (minus 14 degrees Celsius) overnight on Saturday.
In Ottawa, a popular winter festival was all but washed out as rain and high winds ruined outdoor ice sculptures and ended ice-skating on the city's Rideau Canal.
